words.meaningIt: Riflettere profondamente su qualcosa, considerare attentamente.
words.definitionEn: To think carefully about something for a period of time, often before making a decision.
examples: She spent the afternoon pondering the meaning of life.
He paused to ponder his next move in the chess game.
words.exampleIt: Ha passato il pomeriggio a riflettere sul significato della vita.
words.commonMistake: Gli italiani a volte usano "ponder" in modo troppo leggero; implica una riflessione più profonda e prolungata rispetto a un semplice "think".
words.cloze: Before accepting the job offer, she needed a few days to ____ the pros and cons.

words.meaningIt: Capace di riprendersi rapidamente da difficoltà o shock; elastico.
words.definitionEn: Able to return to its original shape after being bent, stretched, or compressed; able to recover quickly.
examples: Children are often very resilient and adapt quickly to new situations.
The economy has proven remarkably resilient despite global challenges.
words.exampleIt: I bambini sono spesso molto resilienti e si adattano rapidamente a nuove situazioni.
words.commonMistake: Non confondere con "resistant" (resistente a qualcosa, es. ai danni). "Resilient" si riferisce più alla capacità di recupero.
words.cloze: After facing several setbacks, the team proved to be incredibly ____ and managed to win the championship.

words.meaningIt: Rendere più facile o possibile un processo o un'azione.
words.definitionEn: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.
examples: The new software will facilitate communication between departments.
A good leader should facilitate discussion, not dominate it.
words.exampleIt: Il nuovo software faciliterà la comunicazione tra i dipartimenti.
words.commonMistake: A volte gli italiani tendono a usare "make easy" o "simplify" quando "facilitate" sarebbe più appropriato in contesti formali di business.
words.cloze: Our goal is to ____ the exchange of ideas among all team members during the workshop.

words.meaningIt: Rendere meno grave, ridurre l'impatto o la severità di qualcosa.
words.definitionEn: To make something less harmful, serious, or painful.
examples: We need to find ways to mitigate the risks associated with this investment.
Emergency measures were put in place to mitigate the effects of the flood.
words.exampleIt: Dobbiamo trovare modi per mitigare i rischi associati a questo investimento.
words.commonMistake: Gli italiani a volte usano "reduce" in contesti formali dove "mitigate" suona più specifico e appropriato per pericoli o problemi gravi.
words.cloze: The company implemented new security protocols to ____ potential cyber threats.

words.meaningIt: Dipendere da qualcuno/qualcosa; fidarsi di qualcuno/qualcosa.
words.definitionEn: To need or depend on someone or something; to trust someone or something.
examples: You can always rely on me for support.
Many people rely on public transport to get to work.
words.exampleIt: Puoi sempre contare su di me per un supporto.
words.commonMistake: Non confondere con "rely to". La preposizione corretta è sempre "on".
words.cloze: In a crisis, it's good to know you have colleagues you can ____ for help.
